_about: The USB Wi-Fi sticks AurOS tells people to buy. A stick is listed only if its CHIP has a driver in the kernel of the AurOS image AND in the newer (HWE) kernel, with the firmware that driver needs in the image: tools/hw/sticks.py checks every id below against hw/compat.json and hw/compat-hwe-wifi.json, writes the list into website/advanced.html (#wifi-sticks) and fails if any page, sentence or help text recommends a stick without naming a chip from this file. Products are examples from public lists of Linux-friendly sticks (morrownr's 'Plug and Play' list on GitHub, and hardware databases for the MT7601U ones); makers change the chip inside a model between versions, so the page tells the reader to buy by the chip and to check the version. NEVER list the Realtek RTL8811AU/8812AU/8821AU/8814AU sticks (see 'avoid').

chips.name: MediaTek MT7921AU
chips.what: newest: Wi-Fi 6 and 6E, 2.4 and 5 GHz, "AX1800" or "AXE3000"

products.name: Fenvi FU-AX1800, only the one whose listing says MT7921 (Fenvi also sells a look-alike with a Realtek chip)

avoid.chips: Realtek RTL8811AU, RTL8812AU, RTL8821AU and RTL8814AU
avoid.examples: the TP-Link Archer T2U Nano and many cheap "AC600" and "AC1200" sticks
avoid.why: their drivers are very new in the kernel and have not been tried on AurOS
